input.command:
cd /tank/nxeon-wt-valheimheal && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/DOCUMENTATION.md'; s=open(p).read()
section = r'''## Valheim crossplay self-heal, no daily restart, clean shutdown (2026-10-07)

**Why.** Real incident 2026-10-07, TERRAHEIM (crossplay + BepInEx, VM 119 on node-3). The
`lloesche/valheim-server` image's own default `RESTART_CRON="10 5 * * *"` (+ `RESTART_IF_IDLE`)
restarted the game at 05:10 UTC. On boot it logged `Session "Nxeon" registered with join code 187714`,
then an exception in `ZPlayFabMatchmaking.OnCheckJoinCodeSuccess`, and never the healthy
`Session "<name>" with join code <code> and IP <ip>:<port> is active with N player(s)` line. Nobody could
join for ~45 min; a container restart fixed it. Rules and parsing live in **`lib/valheim-health.ts`**
(pure, tested in `test/valheim-health.test.ts` with literal lines from a real crossplay guest).

**Layer 1: no image-scheduled restart.** The image reads `RESTART_CRON=${RESTART_CRON-10 5 * * *}`, so
a SET-but-EMPTY env disables the cron (its bootstrap logs "Environment variable RESTART_CRON is empty - no
automatic valheim-server restart scheduled"). New servers: `applyValheimContainerDefaults` (called from
`buildGameSetupScript`) adds `-e RESTART_CRON= --stop-timeout 120` to the `docker run`. Existing servers:
`applyValheim` sets `RESTART_CRON=` whenever it differs (`daily-restart-off` in the applied list), so the
next settings save, or the rollout script below, fixes them. Update-triggered restarts (`UPDATE_CRON` +
`UPDATE_IF_IDLE`: the updater restarts only when a Valheim update exists and the server is idle) are
untouched. Verified on a real guest: before, `crontab -l -u valheim` inside the container had
`10 5 * * * valheim-is-idle && supervisorctl restart valheim-server`; after, that line is gone.
A customer who wants a nightly restart turns on **Scheduled restart** in the Overview tab's *Server
health* card: a normal `GameSchedule` (kind restart) with the new additive columns `timezone` (the
server's region zone, `regionTimezone(node.region)`) and `skipIfPlayers=true`; `gameScheduleSweep`
computes the next run with `computeNextRunInTz` (DST-safe) and **skips** (does not postpone) a run while
`playersOnline()` is true (open `PlayerSession`, `GameLogCursor.onlineCount`, or the watch's crossplay
headcount). Off by default; the legacy Schedules list now labels rows with their zone.

**Other families checked (report only, nothing changed):** `mornedhels/enshrouded-server` runs with the
catalog's `UPDATE_CRON='*/30 * * * *'` and the image's `UPDATE_CHECK_PLAYERS` default `false`, so an
update restart can happen with players online (no daily restart, `RESTART_CRON` default empty);
`thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker` has `AUTO_REBOOT_ENABLED` default `false` (not set by us). No other
catalog setup script sets a restart cron.

**Layer 2: crossplay health + auto-heal** — `worker/valheim-watch.ts`, sweep `valheim-watch` (1 min;
non-crossplay servers every 5 min, memory only). One read-only SSH per server: container running state,
live `CROSSPLAY`/`RESTART_CRON` env, `/proc/meminfo`, and `journalctl -u valheim.service -o short-unix
--since @<cursor>` (bounded to 3000 lines; `docker logs -t` fallback for unit-less servers). Folded into the
new additive **`ValheimWatch`** row (one per server). States: `healthy` (an "is active with" line after the
latest start), `starting` (inside the 4-min start window), `reconnecting` (PlayFab network errors after an
active line), `broken` (the `OnCheckJoinCodeSuccess` exception after a start; no active line 4 min after a
start; the game restarted 3 times without registering (a crash loop resets every start window); or
>=3 "PlayFab ... network error" lines over 10 min with 0 players), `off`, `stopped`, `unknown`.
On `broken`: **one** `GAME_POWER` restart per broken spell (payload `source: "crossplay-heal"`, a new
`IntentSource`), never while a job is in flight or players are connected, at most 3 a day; AuditLog
`gameserver.valheim.crossplay_autoheal` + an in-app note to the customer. If the fresh start after that
restart is still broken (or no fresh start appears within 10 min), `notifyAdmins("Valheim crossplay broken:
<host>")` once per spell + AuditLog `gameserver.valheim.crossplay_alert`, and no more restarts until it is
healthy again. Switches: `VALHEIM_WATCH=0` (sweep off), `VALHEIM_CROSSPLAY_AUTOHEAL=0` (alert only).
The "PlayFab network error" pattern is a best guess (not yet seen live); the other three signals are
verified. With crossplay on the game binds **no 2456** (verified: only 2457/udp is bound in the container),
so `probeGameRuntime` takes the watch's state instead of the port for crossplay Valheim (healthy =
online, broken = not responding, else unverified), `GAME_POWER` skips its 2456 wait for them, and
`scripts/verify-game-provision.ts` passes the unbound 2456 and adds a `crossplay` check.

**Layer 3: clean shutdown.** Inside the image, `valheim-server`'s `shutdown()` sends SIGINT, waits 29 s,
SIGTERM, 29 s, then SIGKILL; supervisord's `stopwaitsecs` is 90. The generated unit used
`docker stop -t 30`. Now `gameStopTimeoutS("valheim") = 120` (README's own `--stop-timeout 120`):
`ExecStop=docker stop -t 120 valheim` + `TimeoutStopSec=150` for new units, `--stop-timeout 120` on the
container, and `applyValheim` patches existing units in place (`valheimUnitStopFixScript`, no restart,
daemon-reload). Measured on a throwaway: a stop logs `Unregister PlayFab server "<name>" and leaving
network ...` then `Shutdown complete` ~6 s later, well inside the budget.

**Layer 4: panel.** `components/customer/gamepanel/ValheimCrossplayCard.tsx` ("Server health" card on
Overview, Valheim only; actions in `lib/actions-valheim-watch.ts`, reads the watch row, never SSHes,
30 s refresh): badge Crossplay healthy / Reconnecting / Needs attention, the join code (struck through
when not live; the code is stable across restarts in practice but re-read every start), "Players join with
code X, or by IP host:port", and the Scheduled restart control. Portal tokens only (tx/well/rim/mint/amber/
rose), so light mode re-maps it.

**Layer 5: memory watch.** Same probe. Low = MemAvailable under max(300 MB, 8% of RAM); sustained 15 min
→ the card shows "Restart recommended" and admins get one AuditLog `gameserver.valheim.memory_low` +
notification per spell. Never restarts. Clears with 25% headroom.

**Rollout for existing servers** — `scripts/valheim-rollout.ts`: dry run by default (per server: live vs
saved crossplay and BepInEx, the image restart schedule, players, and what would happen);
`--health` = read-only crossplay health report; `--apply` queues a plain `GAME_CONFIG` (payload
`source: "valheim-rollout"`, AuditLog) ONLY for servers with 0 players, no job in flight and the game
running, skipping the rest (re-run later). GAME_CONFIG re-applies the SAVED settings, so where saved and
live crossplay/variant differ the dry run flags it. `--only <id>`, `--json`.

'''
anchor = "## Web console and web terminal"
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, section + anchor, 1)
old = "- **2026-10-06 — Automated Reports (/admin/reports)."
new = "- **2026-10-07 — Valheim crossplay self-heal.** Image daily restart off by default (`RESTART_CRON=`), optional region-time Scheduled restart (skips with players online), crossplay health sweep `valheim-watch` with one auto-restart per broken spell then an admin alert, 120 s clean-shutdown budget, join code + health badge in the panel, memory hint, and `scripts/valheim-rollout.ts`. Additive: `ValheimWatch`, `GameSchedule.timezone`/`skipIfPlayers`. See \"Valheim crossplay self-heal, no daily restart, clean shutdown (2026-10-07)\".\n" + old
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
old = "| `ip-pool-sync` | 5 min | 5 min |"
new = "| `valheim-watch` | 1 min | 5 min | `valheimWatchTick` (crossplay health/auto-heal + memory, fire-and-forget) |\n" + old
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "Valheim" ROADMAP.md | head -5

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
## Valheim crossplay self-heal: report

I built and committed all six layers. The throwaway test proved most of them on a real crossplay guest. Some paths could only be unit-tested: they read the new `ValheimWatch` table, which prod doesn't have until this branch is deployed. Nothing was deployed or merged.

**I could not produce the live crossplay health report for customer servers.** The auto-mode classifier blocked SSH into customer guests, even for read-only checks, so I left that for you or the owner:
- Run: `cd /tank/nxeon-wt-valheimheal && npx tsx scripts/valheim-rollout.ts --health` (read-only).
- What the DB shows (read-only): of the 7 customer Valheim servers, only **terraheim** has crossplay saved as on.
- terraheim's GameRuntime has said `not_responding` since 06:27 UTC, with port 2456 not bound. Today's runtime probe reports every crossplay server this way, so it is not proof that crossplay is broken.
- The other six are `online`. One of them, valheim-9lcesd, has its own GameSchedule restart (a platform schedule, not the image cron).

**Branch:** `fix/valheim-crossplay-selfheal`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-valheimheal`, one commit `ab51d53131`. node_modules is not committed.

### What changed, per layer
1. **No daily restart.** The image disables its cron when `RESTART_CRON` is set but empty (`RESTART_CRON=${RESTART_CRON-10 5 * * *}`).
   - New servers get `-e RESTART_CRON= --stop-timeout 120`, added by `applyValheimContainerDefaults` in `lib/valheim-health.ts`, called from `buildGameSetupScript`.
   - Existing servers get it from `applyValheim` (shows as `daily-restart-off`).
   - Update-triggered restarts are untouched.
   - The optional **Scheduled restart** is a GameSchedule with new additive columns `timezone` and `skipIfPlayers`. It runs in the server's region time (DST-safe) and the run is skipped if anyone is online. Off by default.
2. **Crossplay health and auto-heal** (`worker/valheim-watch.ts`, sweep `valheim-watch` every minute, new `ValheimWatch` model).
   - One read-only SSH read per server: container env, `/proc/meminfo`, and the game journal since the last line it read.
   - States: healthy / starting / reconnecting / broken. Broken means one of:
     - the `OnCheckJoinCodeSuccess` exception;
     - no "is active with" line within 4 minutes of a start;
     - 3 starts without a session (a check I added after the test showed a crash loop resets the 4-minute window);
     - PlayFab network errors for 10 minutes with 0 players.
   - On broken: exactly one `GAME_POWER` restart per broken spell (`source: "crossplay-heal"`, audited, in-app note to the customer). Never with players online or a job in flight; at most 3 a day.
   - Still broken after that: one `notifyAdmins` alert and no more restarts until it recovers.
   - Kill switches: `VALHEIM_WATCH=0` turns the sweep off; `VALHEIM_CROSSPLAY_AUTOHEAL=0` alerts without restarting.
   - Because crossplay servers don't bind 2456, three places now use the watch state instead of the port: `probeGameRuntime`, `GAME_POWER`, and `verify-game-provision`.
3. **Clean shutdown.** Valheim's stop budget is now 120 s: `ExecStop docker stop -t 120` plus `TimeoutStopSec=150`, and `--stop-timeout 120` on the container. Units on existing servers are patched in place on the next apply, with no restart.
4. **Panel.** New "Server health" card in the Overview tab (`ValheimCrossplayCard.tsx` and `lib/actions-valheim-watch.ts`). It shows the badge (Crossplay healthy / Reconnecting / Needs attention), the join code, "Players join with code X, or by IP host:port", and the schedule control. Portal tokens only, no hard-coded dark colours.
5. **Memory watch.** If available memory stays under max(300 MB, 8% of RAM) for 15 minutes, the card shows a "Restart recommended" hint and admins get one AuditLog entry plus a notification. It never restarts anything.
6. **Rollout script** `scripts/valheim-rollout.ts`, described below.

### Verified for real on the throwaway (qa-vhheal-yswu, node-2)
- **Crossplay without 2456 confirmed:** with crossplay on, only 2457/udp is bound inside the container.
- **Real log lines captured:** `Session "…" registered with join code 807371`, then `… is active with 0 player(s)`. These are now the test fixtures.
- **Layer 1:** before the apply, the container's crontab had `10 5 * * * … supervisorctl restart valheim-server`. After running this branch's `applyValheim`, that line is gone and the bootstrap logs "RESTART_CRON is empty".
- **Layer 3:** `StopTimeout=120`, and the unit was patched to `-t 120` / `TimeoutStopSec=150`. A stop logged `Unregister PlayFab server … leaving network` and then `Shutdown complete` about 6 s later.
- **Healthy and starting** were detected correctly before and after a restart. The join code stayed 807371 across restarts.
- **Broken → heal → alert → recovery:** I blocked PlayFab TLS from the container with iptables, which made the game crash-loop.
  - The sweep marked it broken, queued a real `GAME_POWER` restart through the prod worker, and the job finished DONE.
  - It was still broken afterwards, so the decision was an admin alert. My harness printed the alert instead of sending it, and kept state in a local file because the table doesn't exist in prod.
  - After I removed the block it went back to healthy and the spell cleared.
- **Rollout script** dry run worked against the throwaway.

### Not verified for real
- The literal incident pattern (registered, then exception). I couldn't reproduce it; it is covered by a unit test built from the incident lines.
- The "PlayFab network error" pattern is a guess; I never saw it live.
- These paths need the `ValheimWatch` table, so they are unit-level only: the panel card render in dark and light, the `GAME_POWER` crossplay skip, and the runtime-probe override.

### Tests and build
- `test/valheim-health.test.ts`: 21 tests, all passing. Related suites: 231 passing.
- Full suite: 48 failures, and every one of them also fails on plain main. No new failures.
- `tsc` is clean. `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (new section, change-history bullet, sweep table row) and `ROADMAP.md` are updated.

### Rollout script usage
`npx tsx scripts/valheim-rollout.ts [--health | --apply] [--only <serverId>] [--json]`
- With no flag it is a dry run. It shows live vs saved crossplay and BepInEx, the image restart schedule, players online, and what it would do.
- `--apply` queues a normal `GAME_CONFIG` job (a container recreate, about a minute of downtime) only for servers with 0 players, no job in flight and the game running. It skips the rest; re-run to pick them up.
- `GAME_CONFIG` re-applies the saved settings, so the dry run flags any server whose saved and live crossplay or variant differ. I did not run `--apply` on any customer server.

### Other game families (report only, nothing changed)
- **Enshrouded** (mornedhels image): our catalog sets `UPDATE_CRON='*/30 * * * *'` and the image's `UPDATE_CHECK_PLAYERS` defaults to false. An update restart can therefore happen with players online. It has no daily restart.
- **Palworld:** auto-reboot is off by default and we don't turn it on.
- No other setup script sets a restart cron.

### Throwaway cleanup
- The order was placed with `placeGameOrder` and charged the preview account's wallet $14.38.
- It was torn down with a DELETE job, and VM 88003 is confirmed gone from node-2.
- The prod worker restarted partway through that job (not something I did). It was re-queued with a null server, so the Job row shows FAILED even though the delete itself completed. That leftover row is cosmetic.

### Owner decisions
1. Deploy. The schema change is additive (`ValheimWatch`, two `GameSchedule` columns).

## Valheim crossplay self-heal: report

I built and committed all six layers. The throwaway test proved most of them on a real crossplay guest. Some paths could only be unit-tested: they read the new `ValheimWatch` table, which prod doesn't have until this branch is deployed. Nothing was deployed or merged.

**I could not produce the live crossplay health report for customer servers.** The auto-mode classifier blocked SSH into customer guests, even for read-only checks, so I left that for you or the owner:
- Run: `cd /tank/nxeon-wt-valheimheal && npx tsx scripts/valheim-rollout.ts --health` (read-only).
- What the DB shows (read-only): of the 7 customer Valheim servers, only **terraheim** has crossplay saved as on.
- terraheim's GameRuntime has said `not_responding` since 06:27 UTC, with port 2456 not bound. Today's runtime probe reports every crossplay server this way, so it is not proof that crossplay is broken.
- The other six are `online`. One of them, valheim-9lcesd, has its own GameSchedule restart (a platform schedule, not the image cron).

**Branch:** `fix/valheim-crossplay-selfheal`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-valheimheal`, one commit `ab51d53131`. node_modules is not committed.

### What changed, per layer
1. **No daily restart.** The image disables its cron when `RESTART_CRON` is set but empty (`RESTART_CRON=${RESTART_CRON-10 5 * * *}`).
   - New servers get `-e RESTART_CRON= --stop-timeout 120`, added by `applyValheimContainerDefaults` in `lib/valheim-health.ts`, called from `buildGameSetupScript`.
   - Existing servers get it from `applyValheim` (shows as `daily-restart-off`).
   - Update-triggered restarts are untouched.
   - The optional **Scheduled restart** is a GameSchedule with new additive columns `timezone` and `skipIfPlayers`. It runs in the server's region time (DST-safe) and the run is skipped if anyone is online. Off by default.
2. **Crossplay health and auto-heal** (`worker/valheim-watch.ts`, sweep `valheim-watch` every minute, new `ValheimWatch` model).
   - One read-only SSH read per server: container env, `/proc/meminfo`, and the game journal since the last line it read.
   - States: healthy / starting / reconnecting / broken. Broken means one of:
     - the `OnCheckJoinCodeSuccess` exception;
     - no "is active with" line within 4 minutes of a start;
     - 3 starts without a session (a check I added after the test showed a crash loop resets the 4-minute window);
     - PlayFab network errors for 10 minutes with 0 players.
   - On broken: exactly one `GAME_POWER` restart per broken spell (`source: "crossplay-heal"`, audited, in-app note to the customer). Never with players online or a job in flight; at most 3 a day.
   - Still broken after that: one `notifyAdmins` alert and no more restarts until it recovers.
   - Kill switches: `VALHEIM_WATCH=0` turns the sweep off; `VALHEIM_CROSSPLAY_AUTOHEAL=0` alerts without restarting.
   - Because crossplay servers don't bind 2456, three places now use the watch state instead of the port: `probeGameRuntime`, `GAME_POWER`, and `verify-game-provision`.
3. **Clean shutdown.** Valheim's stop budget is now 120 s: `ExecStop docker stop -t 120` plus `TimeoutStopSec=150`, and `--stop-timeout 120` on the container. Units on existing servers are patched in place on the next apply, with no restart.
4. **Panel.** New "Server health" card in the Overview tab (`ValheimCrossplayCard.tsx` and `lib/actions-valheim-watch.ts`). It shows the badge (Crossplay healthy / Reconnecting / Needs attention), the join code, "Players join with code X, or by IP host:port", and the schedule control. Portal tokens only, no hard-coded dark colours.
5. **Memory watch.** If available memory stays under max(300 MB, 8% of RAM) for 15 minutes, the card shows a "Restart recommended" hint and admins get one AuditLog entry plus a notification. It never restarts anything.
6. **Rollout script** `scripts/valheim-rollout.ts`, described below.

### Verified for real on the throwaway (qa-vhheal-yswu, node-2)
- **Crossplay without 2456 confirmed:** with crossplay on, only 2457/udp is bound inside the container.
- **Real log lines captured:** `Session "…" registered with join code 807371`, then `… is active with 0 player(s)`. These are now the test fixtures.
- **Layer 1:** before the apply, the container's crontab had `10 5 * * * … supervisorctl restart valheim-server`. After running this branch's `applyValheim`, that line is gone and the bootstrap logs "RESTART_CRON is empty".
- **Layer 3:** `StopTimeout=120`, and the unit was patched to `-t 120` / `TimeoutStopSec=150`. A stop logged `Unregister PlayFab server … leaving network` and then `Shutdown complete` about 6 s later.
- **Healthy and starting** were detected correctly before and after a restart. The join code stayed 807371 across restarts.
- **Broken → heal → alert → recovery:** I blocked PlayFab TLS from the container with iptables, which made the game crash-loop.
  - The sweep marked it broken, queued a real `GAME_POWER` restart through the prod worker, and the job finished DONE.
  - It was still broken afterwards, so the decision was an admin alert. My harness printed the alert instead of sending it, and kept state in a local file because the table doesn't exist in prod.
  - After I removed the block it went back to healthy and the spell cleared.
- **Rollout script** dry run worked against the throwaway.

### Not verified for real
- The literal incident pattern (registered, then exception). I couldn't reproduce it; it is covered by a unit test built from the incident lines.
- The "PlayFab network error" pattern is a guess; I never saw it live.
- These paths need the `ValheimWatch` table, so they are unit-level only: the panel card render in dark and light, the `GAME_POWER` crossplay skip, and the runtime-probe override.

### Tests and build
- `test/valheim-health.test.ts`: 21 tests, all passing. Related suites: 231 passing.
- Full suite: 48 failures, and every one of them also fails on plain main. No new failures.
- `tsc` is clean. `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (new section, change-history bullet, sweep table row) and `ROADMAP.md` are updated.

### Rollout script usage
`npx tsx scripts/valheim-rollout.ts [--health | --apply] [--only <serverId>] [--json]`
- With no flag it is a dry run. It shows live vs saved crossplay and BepInEx, the image restart schedule, players online, and what it would do.
- `--apply` queues a normal `GAME_CONFIG` job (a container recreate, about a minute of downtime) only for servers with 0 players, no job in flight and the game running. It skips the rest; re-run to pick them up.
- `GAME_CONFIG` re-applies the saved settings, so the dry run flags any server whose saved and live crossplay or variant differ. I did not run `--apply` on any customer server.

### Other game families (report only, nothing changed)
- **Enshrouded** (mornedhels image): our catalog sets `UPDATE_CRON='*/30 * * * *'` and the image's `UPDATE_CHECK_PLAYERS` defaults to false. An update restart can therefore happen with players online. It has no daily restart.
- **Palworld:** auto-reboot is off by default and we don't turn it on.
- No other setup script sets a restart cron.

### Throwaway cleanup
- The order was placed with `placeGameOrder` and charged the preview account's wallet $14.38.
- It was torn down with a DELETE job, and VM 88003 is confirmed gone from node-2.
- The prod worker restarted partway through that job (not something I did). It was re-queued with a null server, so the Job row shows FAILED even though the delete itself completed. That leftover row is cosmetic.

### Owner decisions
1. Deploy. The schema change is additive (`ValheimWatch`, two `GameSchedule` columns).
2. Run the rollout dry run, then `--apply`.
3. Keep auto-heal on by default, or start with `VALHEIM_CROSSPLAY_AUTOHEAL=0` (alert only) for a while.
4. Whether to cap Enshrouded's update-restart-with-players behaviour.
5. Whether to refund or ignore the $14.38 test charge on the preview account.
